References associated with a taxon

Source: R/sacha_clb.R
references_sp.Rd

Retrieves the bibliographic references that the configured source links to a species, for example the sources of its taxonomic treatment, synonymy and distribution. Duplicated citations are removed, whitespace inside each citation is normalized, and citations are sorted alphabetically. The references can also be exported to a BibTeX file.

references_sp(species, language = NULL, save_bib = FALSE, bib_dir = ".")

references_sp_md(species, language = NULL, save_bib = FALSE, bib_dir = ".")

Arguments

species

Character scalar with a scientific name of at least a genus and a specific epithet, for example "Bidens andicola". Surrounding and repeated whitespace is removed. Vectors of length greater than one, NA and single-word names are rejected with an error.

language

Language of labels and messages: a YAML basename in inst/lang/ (for example "en" or "es") or a declared alias (for example "english" or "spanish"). NULL (default) uses the language set with sacha_configure(). It does not translate the citation. Unsupported values raise an error.

save_bib

Logical. FALSE (default) only returns or prints the references. TRUE also saves them in BibTeX format as described in Saving references in BibTeX. Any other value raises an error.

bib_dir

Base directory in which sacha_exports/Family_Genus_species is created when save_bib = TRUE. Any valid path, absolute or relative to the working directory, is accepted. Defaults to "." (the working directory), producing files under ./sacha_exports. It is ignored when save_bib = FALSE.

Value

  • references_sp(): a character string with one citation per line, or a localized no-data or connection message.

  • references_sp_md(): invisibly, a Markdown string with a bold localized heading followed by a bulleted list with one citation per item, or "" when no references are available. The string is also written to the console.

Saving references in BibTeX

With save_bib = TRUE, the references are also written to a .bib file inside a directory named after the species with the pattern Family_Genus_species, for example Asteraceae_Bidens_andicola. The directory is created under bib_dir if it does not exist, and the file has the same name as the directory plus the .bib extension:

<bib_dir>/sacha_exports/Asteraceae_Bidens_andicola/Asteraceae_Bidens_andicola.bib

The family is taken from the classification returned by the source; if no family is available, Unknown is used. Characters other than letters and digits are replaced by underscores. An existing file with the same name is overwritten.

When the source provides structured bibliographic metadata (CSL-JSON), each reference becomes a typed BibTeX entry (@article, @book, @incollection, @inproceedings, @techreport or @misc) with authors, title, container, year, volume, issue, pages, publisher, DOI and URL when present. References without structured metadata are written as @misc entries that keep the full citation in the note field. Citation keys are built from the family name of the first author and the year, and are made unique within the file. Nothing is written when the source has no references.

See also

syn_and_comb(), first_publicacion(), sacha_configure(), accessors-sacha

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
references_sp("Bidens andicola")

references_sp("Bidens andicola", language = "es")

references_sp("Bidens andicola", save_bib = TRUE)

references_sp("Bidens andicola", save_bib = TRUE, bib_dir = "bibliografia")

references_sp_md("Bidens andicola")

references_sp_md("Bidens andicola", save_bib = TRUE, bib_dir = "bibliografia")
} # }
